# WILSON FORMATION FORGE v0.25.0

v0.25 closes the first small multi-exchange compiler push. For every 488-word degree-eight dictionary drawn from the 511 words of lengths at most eight, the support-pattern residual machine needs at least **81 primitive calls**. The proof is global: every full transition support graph is complete bipartite `K_{2^k,2^(8-k)-1}`, and 23 omissions are insufficient to reduce any layer except `k=4`; attaining 81 requires deleting a complete 16-word `k=4` fiber.

Using that characterization, the full 30,063,484 two-exchange neighborhood collapses to 2,495,388 structurally admissible 81-call supports. An exhaustive low-rank determinant-proxy screen selects the exchange `HHHHHHG,GHHHHHHH -> HHHGHGHG,HHHGHHGG`. Exact p-adic reconstruction gives the sensor at **4,630 bits** and Paley at **4,596 bits**, both with 488 active words, `(0,2)` native state, and the exact 81-call / 138,572-cost physical residual machine. These save 22/27 bits versus v0.23 and 11/14 bits versus the best v0.24 heights.

V0.25 also turns the engineered Formation-v41 species join into explicit Pareto fronts. Across all 35 triples the rank/bypass front is the four `12/48/*` triples with rank 121 and direct bypass. Among the seven Fano lines, four remain undominated once Wilson rank, EQ bypass, route degree, arithmetic height, word passes and traffic are scored jointly. The species-route map remains an engineered keyspace, not an intrinsic identification.

The canonical reader advances to v0.69 with Part XLV on the global 81-call theorem, two-exchange rational lifts, and the joined finite Pareto calculus.

Packaging note: to keep the distributable archive below the attachment ceiling, v0.25 retains the immediate v0.68 predecessor and current v0.69 reader at the package root; redundant root-level v0.65-v0.67 reader binaries were omitted. Their source/update lineage and all mathematical, code, data, and upstream handoff artifacts remain in the release.

Those reductions are not promoted. The 488/633 programs are exact characteristic-zero certificates on deterministic prefix supports, not a global l0-minimality theorem.

**Formation v38 integral correction.** The v37 outer residual shadow remains binary, but the exact mixed critical center can retain order `2^max(d_i)`. In the full-outer finite-simple v14 universe the complete critical list is: one centerless simple atom; one-species cyclic prime-power central atom; or one multi-species binary all-ones lock on one copy of each species. Arbitrary mixed projective codes, relative p-adic phase, full-support cancellation tethers and criticality-relevant v36 section witnesses disappear only in that stated scope.

**Formation v37 live-state collapse.** Under the full outer action on finite nonabelian simple species, every residual Schur coinvariant is `0` or `C2`. **Arithmetic boundary.** The general task compiler remains expressed in the certified good-prime 127-coordinate coupling model. Choose a degree-nine `G/H` word basis and exact Hecke/native section jointly to minimize coefficient height, nonzero word count, shared-prefix DAG cost, primitive ISA cost and depth. # WILSON FORMATION FORGE v0.20.0

v0.20 solves the first task-adapted section-synthesis problem in the 127-dimensional degree-eight fiber product, imports WILSON-EQ-LAB v0.4.0 as the executable application target and Formation Polarization v31 as the new subspace/criticality handoff, and replaces the previous universal pure-minus schedule by an exact task-dependent Pareto theorem.

**Exact section criterion.** For a Hecke task subspace `T` and native radical subspace `S`, a degree-eight synchronized section exists iff `sigma_H(T)` lies inside `sigma_A(S)`. It can be chosen native-faithful iff, in addition, `dim ker(sigma_A|S) >= dim ker(sigma_H|T)`. At degree nine the synchronized language is the full direct product, so only native dimension remains.

**Full teacher improves from `(0,3)` to `(1,2)`.** One plus plus two minus arrows give native dimension `155`, full coupling-signature rank `127`, and signature-kernel dimension `28`, enough to absorb the Hecke kernel dimension `25`. Thus the complete 152-dimensional teacher has a faithful degree-eight radical section in `(1,2)`. Compared with the old pure-minus `(0,3)` realization, this removes 70 of 225 arrow coordinates and lowers the inherited arrow-operation proxy from 4500 to 3030 with the same three-channel count.

**The real EQ-LAB task is much smaller.** The trainable one-hop Wilson family is the 8-dimensional span of identity plus seven Q192 routes; including the frozen depth-five denoising target gives a 9-dimensional current application span. Their coupling signatures are injective. At degree eight every named nonzero application task requires two minus arrows and no one-minus or plus-only slice contains it. At degree nine the coupling lock disappears: the Paley and C3 lines fit in one plus arrow, while the seven-route bank, 8-dimensional one-hop family and 9-dimensional application span fit faithfully in the two plus arrows, only ten native coordinates.

**Depth is a resource.** The Paley and C3 lines enter the X/Y Hecke language at degree one; the route bank, learned one-hop family, application span and full Hecke algebra enter by degree seven. Pure one-sided radical realization requires degree eight. Spending one further word degree buys complete cross-category independence and can reduce the current application runtime state from a 150-coordinate two-minus code to a 10-coordinate two-plus code.

**Boundary discipline.** EQ-LAB's route/Tanner hard-negative observables are inside the Hecke task family and are covered by these sections. The historical Q2/Q35 and Q159/Q160 canonical-factor semi-invariants remain outside the positive species-3 native category and stay as an external admission gate. V31 is used only as a structural warning that actual subspaces/projective lines matter; no Wilson-formation functor is claimed.

The canonical reader advances to v0.64 with Part XL on exact section criteria, the `(1,2)` full-teacher improvement, the EQ-LAB application Pareto front, and the remaining characteristic-zero height problem.

# WILSON FORMATION FORGE v0.19.0

v0.19 constructs the missing exact bridge between the 486-dimensional native star-transport algebra and the 152-dimensional Q192 Wilson Hecke algebra.  The bridge is not an algebra identification: the same two-letter free language realizes a finite fiber product through degree eight and the complete direct product by degree nine.  Formation Polarization v30 is imported byte-for-byte and its marginal-insufficiency theorem supplies the correct joint-state interpretation.

**Cross-category Chinese remainder.**  Pair native `g,h` with Hecke `X=A_49` and `Y=-A_12-A_48-A_59+A_95+A_116+A_125`.  The synchronized word ranks are `1,3,7,15,31,63,127,255,511,638` through degree nine.  Degree eight has full native rank 486 and full Hecke rank 152 but joint rank only 511; degree nine reaches `638=486+152`, proving that the synchronized image is the full direct product `A_native x H_Wilson`.

**Unit-separating relation.**  The first Hecke relation is `X^4-26X^3-131X^2+300X+900=0`.  The same polynomial evaluated on native `g` is a unit with full `(2,3)` arrow rank.  Hence the primitive generator pairing admits no nonzero common quotient: the two relation ideals are comaximal.  The degree-nine rank theorem gives the sharp finite word depth at which the two sectors become independently addressable.

**Degree-eight cooperative lock.**  The 511-dimensional degree-eight paired image has pure-native dimension 359, pure-Hecke dimension 25, and a residual coupling quotient of dimension 127.  The release freezes explicit 127-component signatures `sigma_A` and `sigma_H` with `sigma_A(a)=sigma_H(h)` on every synchronized degree-eight state.  This is the Wilson analogue of v30's marginal-insufficiency theorem: complete marginals do not imply a complete joint state.

**Relation transduction.**  The 25 native degree-eight relations inject into a 25-dimensional Hecke family whose pairwise products span all 152 Hecke dimensions.  The 359 Hecke relations inject into a 359-dimensional native family with full `(2,3)` channel rank; one left/right multiplication step by `g,h` closes it to all 486 native dimensions.

**Two-minus joint compiler, three-minus native encoding.**  Inside the pure-minus degree-eight slice, retaining 0,1,2,3 fixed minus channels gives Hecke dimensions `25,100,152,152` and native dimensions `0,75,150,225`.  Thus any two fixed minus arrows are necessary and sufficient for a surjective synchronized compiler of every Hecke filter.  But two channels cannot faithfully encode the full 152-dimensional teacher in the native marginal: every section loses at least two dimensions.  All three minus channels admit a faithful native-only linear encoding.  The distinction is exact: two channels are optimal for joint execution; three are required for faithful pure-minus native representation.

The canonical reader advances to v0.63 with Part XXXIX on the cross-category direct-product theorem, the 127-dimensional cooperative lock, relation transduction, and the optimal two-minus joint compiler.

# WILSON FORMATION FORGE v0.18.0

**Twelve native strata.**  Writing the arrow payloads as `U in M2x5` and `V in M3x75`, the closure of rank pair `(r_+,r_-)` has dimension `251 + r_+(7-r_+) + r_-(78-r_-)`.  The full `(2,3)` stratum is Zariski open dense.  The nearest proper rank drop `(1,3)` has codimension 4; complete plus blindness `(0,3)` has codimension 10; a one-step minus drop `(2,2)` already has codimension 73.  Thus lower-rank learned transports are genuine algebraic concentration events rather than generic coefficient sparsity.

**Rank-tomography duality.**  The same pair `(r_+,r_-)` is simultaneously the exact minimum number of common execution channels, the exact minimum shared linear dictionary size for a family, and the number of independent arrow selectors required for linear tomography on the occupied multiplicity spaces.  This is the internal Wilson analogue of the imported v28-v29 selector distinction: reachability/global state and local observability are different invariants.
For multiple named families the exact state refines from the rank pair to the actual occupied subspaces `(R_+,R_-)`; joins are subspace sums and intersections measure channel reuse, so relative alignment is real compiler data.

**Exact filter-access ladder.**  In the evaluated `g,h` word filtration, nontrivial plus-blind filters first appear at degree 3 (a 5-dimensional intersection with family rank `(0,3)`).  Minus-blind filters first appear at degree 7 (dimension 30, family rank `(2,0)`).  The radical is zero through degree 6, then appears in degree 7 with dimension 4 and full family rank `(2,3)`.  Neither pure one-sided radical appears before degree 8; at degree 8 the full radical splits as pure-plus dimension 10 and pure-minus dimension 225.

**B64 exact degree.**  `B64` lies in the pure-minus radical and has zero intersection with `W_<=7`.  Since `W_<=8` is the full algebra, every nonzero `B64` operator has exact evaluated filtered degree 8.  The old degree-nine obstruction therefore sits on a sharply identified degree-eight operator frontier.

**Formation v28-v29 import.**  Both user-supplied releases are bundled byte-for-byte and their own release verifiers pass.  V28 proves primitive-selector orbit tomography and 16/16 `L3(4)` recovery; v29 proves the first residual four-state automaton `0<K<A_even<A_odd`, `U4(3)` inversion, the even-`D_n(q)` graph-swap family, cover collapse and selector bifurcation. # WILSON FORMATION FORGE v0.17.0

v0.17 moves the native five-arrow compiler from presentation theory into representation theory and execution scheduling, and it closes the final two even-primary internal rows in the first `L3(4)` formation branch.

**Native category classification.** The eight-dimensional Morita corner is the hereditary path algebra of a three-vertex quiver with two arrows from the common row vertex to the plus sink and three arrows to the minus sink. Its full representation category is wild because the plus-zero subcategory is the three-Kronecker category. The useful finite invariant is therefore not a catalogue of all indecomposables but the exact `GL2 x GL3` arrow-multiplicity rank of Wilson-generated families.

**Arrow concentration theorem.** The historical generators `g,h`, every nonempty `g/h` word through length eight, and all 485 nonidentity members of the selected exact word basis have full native rank `(2,3)`. In contrast, the distinguished 64-dimensional `B64` boundary has exact family rank `(0,3)`: it is completely plus-blind while still requiring all three minus directions. The full radical has `(2,3)`. This gives the compiler a basis-invariant notion of exact channel deletion.

**Optimal schedules.** Native products share the semisimple `a/A` left prefixes and `S` right suffixes, after which every live arrow reduces independently. Under the frozen dense-operation model the exact binary-product count is `3501 + 30 r_+ + 1500 r_-`. Full transport `(2,3)` costs `8061`; the `B64` family `(0,3)` costs `8001`. These are algebraic operation counts, not timing claims.

**Formation branch closure.** Pullback through faithful `4_1.L3(4)` and `4_2.L3(4)` permutation representations gives selector pattern `(0,2,2)` on each three-class orbit of `A6` and `L3(2)`. The outer order-three automorphism cycles the three classes synchronously, and v24 identifies its action on `2C4^2` with the three-cycle of the nonzero vectors. In one common normalized basis the complete rows are therefore `(2,0),(0,2),(2,2)` for both species. In particular the two formerly open first-class marked rows are both `(2,0)`. The first `L3(4)` simple-section branch now has no unresolved even 2-primary `H_2` data.

The canonical reader advances to v0.61 with Part XXXVII on the wild native category, invariant arrow concentration, exact execution schedules, and the completed `L3(4)` internal-row table.

with `a∈Q`, `A∈M15(Q)`, `S∈M5(Q)`, `b∈M_{1×10}(Q)`, and `B∈M_{15×15}(Q)`.  Hence

`A/J ~= Q × M15(Q) × M5(Q)`, `dim J=235`, `J^2=0`.

This corrects v0.14 terminology: the 450-dimensional minus row-kernel contains the full semisimple `M15` block and is not the Jacobson radical. CTblLib's outer-label conventions identify `2_1` as the central outer involution of `Out(L3(4)) ~= C2×S3`; it acts trivially on the mod-two Schur plane because it centralizes the order-three action that cycles all three nonzero vectors. # WILSON FORMATION FORGE v0.14.0

v0.14 completes the first noncommutative diamond calculation for the two-generator characteristic-zero transport algebra and imports Formation Polarization v22 as the first genuinely biaxial noncyclic Schur-selector branch.

**Wilson presentation completion.** The 25 normalized degree-eight relations do **not** generate the full two-sided kernel. Through degree nine the true filtered relation space has dimension `537`, while the two-sided consequences of the old wall have rank exactly `125`; the first new quotient is therefore `412`-dimensional. It decomposes by the filtration as `26` homogeneous degree-nine syzygies plus a `386`-dimensional boundary quotient. The old one-letter leading image has dimension `100` and projection ranks `(25,36,100)` to the row, plus and minus factors. The 386-dimensional quotient is concentrated in the minus-side radical after quotienting the 64-dimensional old boundary there.

The release deliberately withdraws a tempting but false formulation: the 412-dimensional new obstruction has **no canonical `M5`-module type**. The v0.13 `M5` identification applies only to the filtered degree-eight boundary; that boundary is not a subalgebra, so no `M5` action canonically descends. Instead v0.14 freezes the exact filtered decomposition above.

The diamond completion terminates at degree nine. The package contains 486 normal words of maximum degree eight, 25 degree-eight rewrite rules and a redundant exact rewrite table for all 512 degree-nine monomials at `p=1,000,003`. Modulo the old two-sided ideal, exactly 412 degree-nine rules are new. The 25+412 generators span the complete kernel through degree nine; since every word of length at least nine has a reducible length-nine prefix and the 486 normal-word evaluations are independent, the quotient is exactly the 486-dimensional algebra. These dimension and termination statements lift to characteristic zero by good reduction. Explicit rational coefficients for all 412 new rules are not reconstructed in this release.

**Formation v22.** For `H=L3(4)` with 2-primary multiplier `C4^2`, the inclusions into `M22` and `U4(3)` both induce primitive surjections `C4^2 -> C4`, but the pullback covers lie in inequivalent selector orbits: `4_1.L3(4)` for `M22`, `4_2.L3(4)` for `U4(3)`. Each v17 graph signature has order 16 and with `C4` coefficients permits four of the sixteen target frequencies. The selector orbit therefore contains routing information invisible to multiplier orders, rank, image size and kernel type. v22 does not provide one simultaneous marked basis for both selector rows and does not determine the still-open even 2-primary internal maps `A6/L3(2) -> C4^2`; Forge keeps those as explicit HAP handoff slots.

The canonical reader advances to v0.58 with Part XXXIV on the finite degree-nine presentation and the biaxial Schur selectors.

# WILSON FORMATION FORGE v0.13.0

v0.13 lifts the v0.12 species-3 transport solution algebra from the frozen good prime to **characteristic zero without reconstructing a 486-vector rational nullspace**.  The exact integral Q6 carrier satisfies simple star-context identities: on the plus side `E=0`, `LX=-RX`, `LY=RY`; on the minus side `LX=RX`, `LY=-RY`.  Consequently the stacked context images are exactly `C_+ tensor Q^5` and `C_- tensor Q^5` with context dimensions 2 and 3, source kernels 1 and 15, and one-sided endomorphism dimensions 36 and 475.  Every row action in `M5(Q)` lifts on both sides, giving the exact rational pullback

`End^*(Q6)_Q ~= A_+ x_{M5(Q)} A_-`, `dim=486`.

The good-prime model has the same rank, so its deterministic modular generators lift p-locally to a characteristic-zero generating pair.  The exact word filtration over Q is therefore again `1,3,7,15,31,63,127,255,486`, the center is Q, and the first relation space has dimension 25 in degree eight.  v0.13 identifies that 25-wall precisely: if `R8` is the first filtered relation space, the evaluated degree-eight leading term lies in `ev(F_8) cap ev(F_<=7)`, and the common row-action projection gives an isomorphism

`R8 ~= M5(Q)`.

This is a filtered gluing theorem, not an algebra-isomorphism claim: the 25-dimensional overlap itself is not multiplicatively closed.  The package freezes a normalized modular wall whose 25 boundary images are the 25 M5 matrix units and checks naturality under an invertible homogeneous GL2 change of generators.

v0.13 also imports Formation Polarization v21 byte-for-byte.  The alternating tower is compiled coefficient-universally as `C6 --iso--> C6 --mod2--> C2 --iso--> C2 -> ...` from A6 upward.  The A8-to-A7 marked section has a singleton v17 signature antichain.  This is a new complete formation branch; it does not silently resolve the still-open even 2-primary `L3(4)->A6/L3(2)` maps.

# WILSON FORMATION FORGE v0.8.0 — certificate-aware transport and cyclic critical control

v0.8 imports Formation Polarization v15.0.0 as the authoritative formation-criticality layer and replaces the v0.7 surrogate transport teacher by a certificate-aware teacher whose equality classes are exactly the 271 characteristic-zero Wilson transport classes.  The imported v15 theorem gives the canonical cyclic common-centre phase diagram, the exact proper-factor generation number `rho in {1,2,infinity}`, the higher-2-power valuation tether, and the section-incidence boundary.  The object-level Fourier character group remains separate from the formation compiler state.

The first cross-theorem consequence is a strict improvement over the old binary Hamming hardware frontier.  Every three Q192 routes generate the full 152-dimensional Wilson commutant.  A canonical common-centre controller with multiplier `C_n` has `n` object-level Fourier frequencies.  For prime-power `n`, an all-distinct three-species controller is formation-critical, so it can be coupled to any Wilson route triple without losing formation irreducibility.  Choosing a cheapest triple containing route 49 gives route degree 150.  Therefore 4, 8, and 16 cyclic Fourier frequencies can be supported at degree 150 rather than the binary-Hamming minima 270, 330, and 390.  The savings are 44.44%, 54.55%, and 61.54% in route degree.  The fusion groups are different (`C_4`,`C_8`,`C_16` versus binary subspaces), so this is a hardware/frequency-count comparison, not an identification of the nonlinear algebras.

For `n=2^e`, `e>=2`, v15 also supplies three unique-double critical variants on every three-route support at the same route cost and frequency count, provided the selected formation palette is section-separated or its Schur section-incidence category certifies the required unit-reservoir obstruction.  For non-prime-power `n`, no canonical mixed controller is critical: the compiler emits `rho=1` or `rho=2` instead.  These cases are frozen in `DATA/FORMATION/cyclic_critical_wilson_frontier_v15.json` and exposed by `modules/formation_code/cyclic_phase_v15.py`.

The certificate-aware teacher is constructed from the proof mechanisms of the 279-to-271 characteristic-zero theorem rather than from component IDs.  It uses nine context-species coordinates, the canonical factor dimensions and projective determinant semi-invariants in species 1 and 2, the exact common transport target for species 3, and identity-Hom coordinates for the discrete species 4 through 6.  Direct verification shows that equality of the resulting 66-coordinate vectors on the 279 successful Wilson types gives exactly the frozen 271 components.

All 67 binary Hamming/Theta states are rerun with the same 152-dimensional Wilson spatial packet.  In every species-3 fold the held object is excluded entirely from fitting.  A species-balanced ridge map is trained from Wilson+Schur features to the exact certificate coordinates; regularization is chosen only from known exact positive transports.  The best binary states by Schur dimension are: `k=0` ranks `(2,1,4,250)` and MRR `0.4385`; `k=1` state 9 gives the same ranks at degree 210; `k=2` state 18 gives `(2,1,3,250)`, MRR `0.4593333333`, and the exact minimum hardware degree 270; `k=3` state 53 ties that MRR at the minimum degree 330; and the full 16-frequency `k=4` state falls to ranks `(2,13,14,250)` and MRR `0.1630879121`.

This corrects the interpretation of v0.7.  The earlier positive-difference teacher favored a C3-free degree-300 state.  Once the target is the exact proof-certificate geometry, the best `k=2` and `k=3` states move back onto the minimum hardware frontier and include route 49, partially aligning transport learning with the v0.5 compiler results.  But the stronger negative result survives: no present Schur sidecar learns the entire relation quotient.  `Q107` remains rank 250 in every best dimension-class model.  Generic central-frequency capacity is therefore not the missing theorem signal; the model needs the star-graded relation representation itself.

The embedded v15 archive is byte-preserved at `SOURCE/FORMATION_V15/formation-polarization-theorem-v15.0.0.zip`, and its strip-factor regression is rerun independently.  The canonical reader advances to v0.52 with a new Part XXVIII covering the v15 phase diagram, cyclic frequency compression, the exact 271-class certificate teacher, and the revised section-incidence/transport frontier.

## Inherited v0.7 record


v0.7 imports Formation Polarization v14.0.0 as the authoritative formation layer and runs the exact 67-state C2/Hamming architecture lattice against a relation-aware transport teacher while holding Wilson spatial expressivity fixed at 152 dimensions. Formation control is no longer hard-coded to binary multipliers. The generic state is `Theta=(S,(R_i),C)`: species support, Gamma-stable local coefficient reservoirs, and the global coinvariant code. Join and generated membership are componentwise union/subgroup-sum/subgroup-containment. The full object-level central character code remains the Fourier runtime state; `Theta` remains the lossless formation compiler state. The old 67 Hamming states are retained deliberately as the clean C2 slice of this more general v14 interface.

The main numerical experiment evaluates all 67 canonical Hamming/Theta states. Every state receives the same normalized 152-dimensional Wilson spatial feature packet. A state of Schur dimension `k` adds only its exact `2^k`-frequency Walsh sidecar. In each leave-one-species-3 fold, the teacher is built from exact known positive transports by quotienting the span of their feature differences; the held positive transport is then ranked against one representative of each of the 271 exact characteristic-zero components. The certified hard negatives `Q2/Q35` and `Q159/Q160` are evaluation-only and never used to build the quotient.

The result is non-monotone. No state at any `k=0,1,2,3,4` achieves theorem-level top-1 zero-shot transport: all five dimension classes score `0/4`. Approximate retrieval peaks at `k=2`, four Schur frequencies. Its best state is index 33 with route support `(12,125,48,59,95)`, one-pass route degree 300, held ranks `(8,3,2,120)`, and MRR `0.24166666666666664`. The best `k=1` state has MRR `0.1331956289978678`; the best `k=3` state has `0.18452950558213718`; the full 16-frequency `k=4` state has only `0.13293650793650794` with ranks `(4,9,6,252)`. Therefore 16 Schur frequencies are neither sufficient for exact zero-shot transport nor necessary for the best approximate ranking under this frozen teacher.

The exact hardware minimum frontier remains `150,270,330,390` route degree for `k=1,2,3,4`. The best transport-ranking states occur at the slightly larger costs `180,300,360,390`. Twenty-two smaller states numerically dominate the full `k=4` state in the frozen `(top1,MRR)` comparison; the smallest is a `k=1` state of cost 180. The strongest state, `k=2` index 33, retains at least `95.059%` of the standardized hard-negative distance after the positive-transport quotient, so its ranking improvement is not obtained by simply collapsing the certified negatives.

The focused exact relation audit explains why the numerical teacher cannot be confused with the theorem. At prime `1,000,003`, the complete 121-projective-pencilled rank fingerprint is identical for `Q6,Q7,Q57,Q58,Q107`; it is also identical on `Q2/Q35` and on `Q159/Q160`. The stronger frozen characteristic-zero good-reduction semi-invariants separate both hard-negative pairs. Thus pencil equality is a legitimate positive relation signal but not a complete transport invariant. The next teacher must ingest the canonical factors/semi-invariants themselves, not merely more Schur frequencies.

This produces a useful cross-domain negative result. v0.5 compiler arithmetic favored Fano triples containing the cheaper `C3` route 49. In the present numerical transport benchmark, the best `k=2` and `k=3` states exclude route 49, and the mean MRR of nonzero states without route 49 exceeds that of states containing it. There is therefore no evidence yet for one universal Wilson/formation architecture simultaneously optimizing transport learning and exact compilation. That tension is now a first-class Forge benchmark rather than something hidden by cherry-picking one objective.

The nested v14 archive is byte-preserved at `SOURCE/FORMATION_V14/formation-polarization-theorem-v14.0.0.zip`, SHA-256 `b121c368d2e45013aa3a6be8d35e883881138eb33a6b9a41f3e121cb455d03e4`. Its compiler and stable-strip regression are rerun by the v0.7 gate. The canonical Wilson reader advances to v0.51 with a new Part XXVII covering the arbitrary-multiplier formation interface, the exact 67-state experimental contract, the non-monotone frequency result, the focused five-context audit, and the revised relation-aware frontier.


## Inherited v0.6 record


v0.6 imports Formation Polarization v13.0.0 as the authoritative formation layer and keeps the v0.5 Wilson learning/compiler results intact. The central distinction is now exact. A perfect mixed central object has `X=U_m/K` with full object-level character code `D_X=K^perp`; this is the Fourier-frequency space used by Wilson x central-state equivariant computation. Formation reachability does not require the full `D_X`. It is classified by the lossless compiler state

`Theta(X)=(S_X,A_X,C_X)`, with `supp(C_X) <= A_X <= S_X`,

where `S` is simple support, `A` is central-activity support, and `C` is the block-parity image of `D`. For perfect objects the generated-formation join is exactly union/union/span. The new activity coordinate fixes the parity-only ambiguity between a centerless simple factor and an even two-copy amalgam. The imported v13 theorem also closes repeated-amalgam criticality: a common-center `A_m` is formation-critical exactly when every nonzero multiplicity is one, or `m=2e_i` for one species.

The executable Forge now preserves both levels. `modules/formation_code/normal_form.py` implements the finite F2 side of the v13 normal form and joins. The existing 16-frequency Hamming/Walsh sidecar remains the object-level `D` layer, so nonlinear fusion still obeys exact character conservation `d_out=d_1+...+d_q`. The new `Theta` layer is used for symbolic architecture reachability and canonicalization, not as a replacement for the Fourier channels.

The first Forge consequence is an exact architecture quotient. The Hamming `[7,4,3]` layer has 15 nonzero critical Schur atoms. A naive subset search has `2^15=32768` choices. Under the v13 join theorem, selections with the same span have the same formation state. The four-dimensional Hamming space has exactly `1+15+35+15+1=67` subspaces, so the formation-native architecture search collapses `32768 -> 67`, a factor of about `489.075`. The seven weight-three codewords are the support-minimal Fano atoms, but all fifteen nonzero Hamming words have all-distinct canonical critical representatives under v13.

This quotient combines sharply with the v0.4 Wilson route theorem. The seven Hamming coordinates are coupled to Q192 routes `(49,12,125,48,116,59,95)`. Every nonzero Hamming subspace has support at least three, while every three-route subset of Q192 generates the entire 152-dimensional Wilson commutant over Q by degree five. Hence all 66 nonzero `Theta` states retain full Wilson spatial linear expressivity. Central-frequency capacity and hardware route cost can therefore be varied without sacrificing spatial equivariant closure.

The exact support frontier is the generalized Hamming-weight hierarchy `3,5,6,7`. With route 49 of valency 30 and the six C7 routes of valency 60, the weighted minimum one-pass route degrees for Schur dimensions `1,2,3,4` are `150,270,330,390`, corresponding to `2,4,8,16` Fourier frequencies. On 7,392 Wilson states these cost at least `1,108,800`, `1,995,840`, `2,439,360`, and `2,882,880` directed edge visits per scalar pass. The minimizer counts are `3,15,6,1`. These figures are frozen in `DATA/FORMATION/hamming_theta_lattice_v13.json`.

The v0.5 271-class benchmark and compiler Pareto front remain unchanged. Strict unseen species-3 transport is still not solved by ordinary spatial equivariance or Schur-frequency legality alone; the best frozen results remain the exact-Schur sidecar improvement and the transport-consistency ranks recorded in v0.5. Likewise, the current compiler Pareto pair remains `(49,12,125)` for coefficient height and `(49,48,116)` for route traffic / short transport discrimination. v13 strengthens the search loop by giving it an exact formation-state quotient, not by retroactively changing those numerical learning results.

The nested `SOURCE/FORMATION_V13/formation-polarization-theorem-v13.0.0.zip` is byte-preserved with SHA-256 `aeed6508484811c084a2780ee6f2dc13d0559b5a4adcab161e977e1955b77945`. Its theorem ledger and proof audit are also copied alongside the archive. The v12 and v11 packages remain embedded as historical predecessors.

The canonical Wilson reader is advanced to v0.50. The new Part XXVI records the mixed-central normal form, the exact distinction between `D` and `Theta`, the 67-state architecture quotient, the generalized-weight hardware frontier, the critical-atom interpretation, and the revised Forge program. The Wilson/formation route identification remains an engineering coupling: v0.6 does not claim that the two source groups are intrinsically the same object.
